description: This challenge focuses on developing health monitoring software to track astronauts’ physical and mental health during space missions. The system can monitor vital signs, detect potential health risks, and provide timely alerts to support astronauts’ safety and well-being in space.
summary: ORBITAL is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage platform designed for long-duration spaceflight. Built on NASA-STD-3001 clinical standards and real-time NASA space weather telemetry, it tracks crew vital signs, predicts microgravity-induced deconditioning, and evaluates cognitive workload using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX).
details:
ORBITAL - Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring & Mission Clinical Triage:

ORBITAL is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage prototype built by Team NUVION for the Health & Performance in Space / Space Exploration challenge.

As human missions venture beyond Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) toward the Moon and Mars, communication latency (up to 22 minutes each way) eliminates real-time medical support from Earth-based flight surgeons. ORBITAL bridges this gap by providing onboard, continuous biometric surveillance and automated clinical decision support:

  • Continuous Biometric Telemetry: Tracks live crew vitals—including Heart Rate, SpO₂, Core Body Temperature, and Respiration—using a live simulation physics engine.
  • Smart Anomaly Rule Engine: Automatically evaluates biometric streams against clinical thresholds to flag life-threatening conditions such as hypoxia, compensatory tachycardia, and space fever the moment they occur.
  • Dual-Role Mission Workflow: Synchronizes two dedicated operational views—a 1-Click Crew Wellness Check-In (logging Space Motion Sickness, cephalic fluid shifts, and sleep quality) and a Chief Flight Surgeon Triage Pipeline featuring tiered alerts (Info, Warning, Critical), one-tap alert acknowledgment, and automated PDF/CSV clinical debrief manifests.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Crew Resilience: Empowers astronauts on Artemis, Lunar Gateway, and deep-space Mars missions to detect and triage medical anomalies independently when disconnected from ground control.
  • Reduced Cognitive & Operational Load: Replaces manual vital tracking with automated anomaly prioritization and structured check-ins, saving critical crew time during high-workload mission phases.
  • Scalable Architecture: Designed to be wearable-sensor agnostic and adaptable from current LEO stations to future deep-space habitats with offline edge-AI clinical copilot capabilities.

Tools, Technologies & NASA Open Data Used

  • Frontend & Simulation: Built as a responsive, interactive web prototype using React and TypeScript, featuring real-time multi-crew telemetry charts, alert triage pipelines, and live biometric simulation physics.
    • NASA-STD-3001: Calibrated clinical alert thresholds and the 600 mSv career radiation dose budget to official NASA Space Flight Human-System Standards.
    • NASA DONKI API: Integrates real-time space weather telemetry (Solar Flares, Coronal Mass Ejections, and Solar Energetic Particles) to anticipate Extravehicular Activity (EVA) radiation hazards.
    • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Grounded physiological baselines in open spaceflight datasets, including the NASA Twins Study (OSD-137) and cardiovascular deconditioning datasets (OSD-379).
    • NASA-TLX: Incorporates the 6-scale NASA Task Load Index to monitor crew cognitive workload alongside physical health.
